verdict.headline: Stocks close at a record as tame wholesale prices cool fears of another Fed rate hike
verdict.label: HOLD — 3 of 6 breached: 30Y 5.24% (15th session above 5.00%); WTI $82.11 and Brent $87.92 both above oil triggers; S&P record; September odds 32%; NVDA reclaims $225; AMAT AH −3.1% on beat+strong guide confirms altitude ceiling
verdict.rationale_short: July PPI (0.0% vs. +0.2% expected) resolved the morning's binary in the Bull direction: the S&P 500 set a record, September hike odds fell to 32%, and NVDA closed above $225 resistance for the first time. Where the morning underestimated: CSCO extended its total sell to −8.5% ($113.39 from $123.88), and AMAT fell ~3.1% AH on a mixed Q3 (EPS beat, revenue slight miss) despite a strong Q4 guide of $10.25B — altitude ceiling now confirmed across networking and semiconductor equipment simultaneously. The 30Y at 5.24% (15th session above 5.00%) is unchanged after two consecutive soft inflation prints. Level that changes the read: 30Y closes below 5.10% before Jackson Hole AND September odds hold below 28%.

trade_setups.asset: NVDA ahead of August 26 — altitude ceiling confirmed across networking and semi-equipment
trade_setups.thesis: NVDA closed at $225.30, above the $225 resistance that capped the prior session. AMAT's AH result updated the setup: EPS beat, strong Q4 guide ($10.25B), still down ~3.1% AH to $517.78. The altitude ceiling is real across both the networking layer (CSCO) and semiconductor equipment (AMAT) — every adjacent AI infrastructure print has now sold on strong results. The bar for NVDA is beating by enough to change the institutional prior, not merely meeting gross margin above 76% and guide above consensus.
trade_setups.entry: $225 is now proven support via today's close; $216 is structural support below. A close above $227 before August 26 extends the reclaim; a return below $221 re-establishes the ceiling setup entering the print.
trade_setups.invalidation: NVDA AH holds above $228 on a materially better-than-expected print, with 30Y below 5.15% entering the August 26 call.
trade_setups.horizon: Through August 26 earnings and Jackson Hole keynote August 27-29.

trade_setups.asset: 30Y Yield — 15 sessions above 5.00% despite two soft prints
trade_setups.thesis: CPI core 2.5% and PPI flat — two consecutive below-expected inflation readings — and the 30Y has compressed only 1bp to 5.24%. The bond market's prior has not broken. Jackson Hole (August 27-29) is the next venue. If Warsh's keynote validates the 30Y's persistence citing annual CPI above 4%, SPR at 40-year lows, and Hormuz as a persistent supply risk, the 30Y is not compressing before year-end. If the speech confirms patience given the CPI/PPI trajectory, the path to 5.10% opens.
trade_setups.entry: 30Y at 5.24%, 15th session above 5.00%. Below 5.20% on two consecutive closes is the first de-escalation signal. Above 5.28% re-establishes the rate overhang.
trade_setups.invalidation: 30Y closes below 5.10% on two consecutive sessions — the formal trigger clears.
trade_setups.horizon: Through Jackson Hole keynote August 27-29 and the September 18 FOMC meeting.

trade_setups.asset: SPCX — August 20 tranche with oil triggers still active
trade_setups.thesis: SPCX at $142.31 has absorbed the PPI-driven rate relief. Both oil triggers remain active: WTI $82.11 and Brent $87.92. Hormuz transit volumes at 8-15/day vs. 130 pre-war and SPR below 300M barrels make oil-side de-escalation dependent on genuine diplomatic progress, not rhetoric. The August 20 tranche (~$8.65B eligible) is the next supply gate.
trade_setups.entry: SPCX $142.31. Absorption thesis: continued close above $128. Front-run signal: close below $120 on elevated volume before August 20.
trade_setups.invalidation: WTI closes below $79 on two consecutive sessions, removing the primary oil trigger ahead of the tranche.
trade_setups.horizon: Through August 20 tranche and October Q3 earnings.

bear_case: The 30Y at 5.24% after flat PPI and 2.5% CPI core is the bond market's explicit statement that two months of below-consensus inflation data do not move its prior. With SPR below 300 million barrels (lowest since January 1983) and Hormuz transits at 8-15/day vs. 130 pre-war, an oil supply disruption is ongoing and will eventually surface in services inflation data. CSCO's cumulative −8.5% sell and AMAT's ~−3.1% AH decline to $517.78 on strong forward guidance confirm that the altitude ceiling now applies across both networking and semiconductor equipment simultaneously — sharpening the NVDA risk entering August 26. If Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote reads the 30Y's persistence as the appropriate market equilibrium given these supply conditions, September odds stabilize above 35% and today's equity record becomes the near-term ceiling. The SPX read no longer holds if it closes below 7,600.
